- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.8), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sharp upward spikes in sentiment (e.g., +1.13 or higher); add 3–7% buffer to forecast following such events.
- Model overestimates in early forecast windows (e.g., first 5–7 days of 30d) when sentiment is volatile; apply downward correction of 3–8% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong mean-reversion pattern (e.g., recent highs followed by sharp drops), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment’s recent 3–5 day average.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model often misses downward trend; apply 5–10% downward adjustment if sentiment is negative over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is flat or neutral (±0.2) over last 5 days, model tends to overfit recent history; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast.
